_meta.note: Binary packet examples from the spec. Hex bytes are space-separated; each example includes field annotations.

examples.name: Pre-Login Request

annotations.desc: Type=0x12 PRELOGIN, Status=0x01 EOM, Length=0x002F(47), SPID=0, PacketID=1, Window=0
Entries: VERSION(0x00), ENCRYPTION(0x01), INSTOPT(0x02), THREADID(0x03), MARS(0x04) each with Offset+Length, terminated by 0xFF
0x00=ENCRYPT_OFF, 0x01=ENCRYPT_ON, 0x02=ENCRYPT_NOT_SUP, 0x03=ENCRYPT_REQ; bit 0x80=ENCRYPT_CLIENT_CERT (0x80/0x81/0x83), bit 0x20=ENCRYPT_EXT (reserved). Checked against MS-TDS 2.2.6.5, June 2026.

notes: Pre-Login is the first message in TDS 7.x after TCP connect
For TDS 8.0, TLS is established at TCP level BEFORE PRELOGIN
VERSION field in PRELOGIN response is used by client to determine if DoneRowCount is LONG or ULONGLONG

examples.name: Login Request (LOGIN7)

annotations.desc: Type=0x10 LOGIN7, Status=0x01 EOM, Length=0x0090(144)
DWORD: total LOGIN7 structure length (not counting packet header)
e.g. 0x74000004 for TDS 7.4, little-endian
Requested packet size (e.g. 0x00001000 = 4096)
Client program version
Client process ID
Connection ID (0 for initial)
fByteOrder(0x01), fChar(0x02), fFloat(0x0C), fDumpLoad(0x10), fUseDB(0x20), fDatabase(0x40), fSetLang(0x80)
fLanguage(0x01), fODBC(0x02), fTransBoundary(0x04), fCacheConnect(0x08), fUserType(0x70), fIntSecurity(0x80)
fSQLType(0x0F), fOLEDB(0x10), fReadOnlyIntent(0x20)
fChangePassword(0x01), fSendYukonBinary(0x02), fUserInstance(0x04), fUnknownCollationHandling(0x08), fExtension(0x10=FeatureExt present)
Minutes offset from UTC (little-endian INT32)
Client locale ID
HostName, UserName, Password, AppName, ServerName, Extension, CltIntName, Language, Database, ClientID(6 bytes MAC), SSPI, AttachDBFile, ChangePassword

notes: Password is XOR-obfuscated: each byte b → ((b & 0x0F) << 4 | (b & 0xF0) >> 4) ^ 0xA5
fExtension=0x10 in OptionFlags3 means FeatureExt is present (after offsets table)
FeatureExt is at offset given by Extension field in offset table
For SPNEGO/Windows auth: fIntSecurity=0x80 in OptionFlags2, SSPI field contains Kerberos/NTLM token

examples.name: Login Request with Federated Authentication
notes: Same as LOGIN7 but includes FeatureExt with FEDAUTH feature (FeatureId=0x02)
FEDAUTH FeatureData: Library(1 byte) + bFedAuthLibrary option bits + optional nonce
If bFedAuthLibrary requires server info: server sends FEDAUTHINFO token first, then client sends Federated Auth Token (packet 0x08)
If bFedAuthLibrary can acquire token independently: token sent with initial LOGIN7

annotations.desc: Database name changed (e.g. to 'testdb')
Language changed
Collation changed (5-byte collation value)
Interface=0x01(SQL), TDSVersion(4B), ProgName(B_VARCHAR), ProgVersion(4B)
Status=0x00 (no more results), CurCmd=0x00, DoneRowCount=0

examples.name: Login Response with Federated Authentication
notes: FEATUREEXTACK contains FeatureId=0x02 (FEDAUTH) acknowledgement
FEATUREEXTACK is terminated with 0xFF
FeatureExtAck entries: FeatureId(1B) + FeatureDataLen(4B) + FeatureData

examples.name: SQL Batch Client Request

annotations.desc: Type=0x01 SQLBatch, Status=0x01 EOM, Length=0x005C(92)
22 bytes total (but spec example shows 0x16=22; note: can be 22 bytes for minimal header)
18 bytes for this Transaction Descriptor header
0x0002 = Transaction Descriptor
8-byte ULONGLONG. 0 = not in explicit transaction; ENVCHANGE type 8 provides this value when BEGIN TRAN is used
1 = one open request on this connection
UTF-16LE encoded SQL string (no length prefix)

notes: ALL_HEADERS is required for SQLBatch, RPC, and TransactionManager requests
For non-transactional requests: TransactionDescriptor = 0x0000000000000000
For requests inside a transaction: use TransactionDescriptor from ENVCHANGE type 8

examples.name: SQL Batch Server Response

annotations.desc: Count=1, col: UserType=0, Flags=0x09 (fNullable+fReadOnlyIntent), TypeName=VARCHAR(3), ColName=''
One row: varchar data 'foo' (3 bytes, Windows-1252/Latin-1)
Status=0x10 (DONE_COUNT), CurCmd, RowCount=1

notes: COLMETADATA precedes every result set
ROW token followed immediately by column data per TYPE_INFO rules
DONE_COUNT (0x10) bit set means RowCount field is valid

examples.name: RPC Client Request

annotations.desc: Type=0x03 RPC, Status=0x01 EOM, Length=0x002F(47)
Same Transaction Descriptor header as SQLBatch
Either US_VARCHAR proc name ('foo3') OR USHORT(0xFFFF) + USHORT ProcID for special stored procs
USHORT: 0x0000=normal, 0x0001=WITH RECOMPILE, 0x0002=NO METADATA, 0x0004=REUSE METADATA
Zero or more RPC parameters: ParamName(B_VARCHAR) + StatusFlags(1B, 0x01=OUTPUT, 0x02=DEFAULT) + TYPE_INFO + value

notes: Use 0xFFFF + ProcID for well-known special stored procedures
ParamName is B_VARCHAR (1-byte length prefix, UTF-16LE); empty string means unnamed parameter
OUTPUT parameters: StatusFlags bit 0x01 set; server returns RETURNVALUE tokens

annotations.desc: Intermediate DONE for each statement inside the proc; Status=0x01 (DONE_MORE)
4-byte INT32 return value of stored procedure
Final DONE for the procedure; Status=0x00 (final)

examples.name: Attention Request

annotations.desc: Type=0x06 ATTENTION, Status=0x01 EOM, Length=0x0008(8) — header only, no payload

notes: Attention is ONLY a packet header — 8 bytes total, no payload
Server responds with DONE token with Status having DONE_ATTN bit (0x20) set
Pre-SQL Server 7.0: attention was 1-byte out-of-band message containing 'A'
TDS 7.x+: attention is in-band using ATTENTION packet type (0x06)

examples.name: SSPI Message
notes: Used in SPNEGO (Windows Integrated Authentication) flows
Contains SSPI token for Kerberos or NTLM exchange step 2+
First SSPI exchange is inside the LOGIN7 message; subsequent exchanges use packet type 0x11

examples.name: SQL Command with Binary Data (Bulk Load)

annotations.desc: Type=0x07 BulkLoadBCP, Status=0x01 EOM, Length=0x0026(38)
Defines columns for the bulk load. bit column: UserType=0, Flags, TypeId=0x32 (BITTYPE/FIXEDLENTYPE 1 byte)
ROW token (0xD1) + data for each row defined by COLMETADATA; no DONE token mid-stream
Status=0x10 DONE_COUNT + RowCount

flow: Client → Server: BulkLoadBCP packet(s) with COLMETADATA + ROW* + DONE
Server → Client: Tabular Result: DONE (rows affected)

examples.name: Transaction Manager Request

annotations.desc: Type=0x0E Transaction Manager Request
Transaction Descriptor header
USHORT: TM_BEGIN_XACT=0x0005, TM_COMMIT_XACT=0x0007, TM_ROLLBACK_XACT=0x0008, TM_SAVEPOINT=0x0009, TM_RELEASE=0x000A, TM_RESETCONN=0x000E, TM_PROMOTE_XACT=0x0016 (example in §4.13)
Depends on RequestType: TM_BEGIN_XACT has IsolationLevel(1B) + Name(B_VARCHAR); TM_PROMOTE_XACT has no payload; TM_COMMIT_XACT has Flags

notes: TM_PROMOTE_XACT (0x0016) promotes local transaction to distributed (DTC)
TM_BEGIN_XACT response: ENVCHANGE type 8 (new transaction descriptor) + DONE
TM_COMMIT_XACT response: ENVCHANGE type 9 (commit) + DONE
TM_ROLLBACK_XACT response: ENVCHANGE type 10 (rollback) + DONE

examples.name: TVP Insert Statement

fields.desc: UserType(ULONG) + Flags(USHORT) + TYPE_INFO + ColName(B_VARCHAR) [+ optional tokens like TVP_ORDER_UNIQUE, TVP_COLUMN_ORDERING]

tvp_structure.TVP_ROW: 0x01 — each row: data for each column per TYPE_INFO
tvp_structure.TVP_NULL_TOKEN: 0xFFFF in Count field of TVP_COLMETADATA indicates NULL TVP (no rows)

notes: TVP is sent as an RPC parameter with type 0xF3
TVP_COLMETADATA precedes row data
Row data follows: TVP_ROW(0x01) + column values
TVP_END_TOKEN(0x00) terminates the TVP data stream

examples.name: SparseColumn Select Statement

annotations.desc: Column with fSparseColumn flag: Flags |= 0x0400 (bit 10). Type is XML (0xF1 XMLTYPE). ColName is typically '__$sparse_columns'
XML value encoded as PLP (Partially Length-Prefixed). TotalLength field can be 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE (unknown length).
Used instead of ROW when NBCROW feature is negotiated. NULL bitmap precedes column data.

sparse_column_flags.fSparseColumn: 0x0400 in Flags — column is a sparse column
sparse_column_flags.fSparseColumnSet: 0x0800 in Flags — column is the sparse column set (XML representation of all sparse cols)

notes: SparseColumn requires NBCROW feature support (TDS 7.3+)
SQL Server 2008 TDS version 0x03000A73 does NOT support NBCROW and fSparseColumnSet
PLP data: 8-byte TotalLength + repeated (4-byte ChunkLen + data) chunks, ChunkLen=0 terminates

fields.desc: StateId(1B) + StateLen(USHORT) + StateValue(StateLen bytes), repeated; terminated when no more entries

examples.name: FeatureExtAck with SESSIONRECOVERY
notes: FEATUREEXTACK token (0xAE) contains server's acknowledgement of SESSIONRECOVERY
FeatureData contains server's SessionStateDataSet for all recoverable states
Client uses this to restore session state on reconnect

sessionstate_structure.desc: Total byte count of all StateId+StateLen+StateValue entries
0x00=Not changed (recovery unnecessary), 0x01=Dirty (state changed), 0x02=Recovery not possible (must reconnect)

subsections.name: Multi-Result SQL Batch
subsections.example_sql: SELECT x FROM t1; UPDATE t2 SET y=1; SELECT z FROM t3
subsections.token_stream: COLMETADATA → ROW* → DONE(MORE|COUNT) → DONE(MORE|COUNT) → COLMETADATA → ROW* → DONE(COUNT)
notes: DONE_MORE bit (0x01) set for intermediate results
DONE_COUNT bit (0x10) set when RowCount is valid
The UPDATE produces a DONE with row count but no COLMETADATA/ROW tokens

subsections.name: Attention Signal (out-of-band cancel)
flow: Client → Server: ATTENTION packet (0x06, 8 bytes, simultaneous)
Server → Client: Partial results (if any) + DONE with DONE_ATTN (0x20) status
subsections.done_attn_bits: DONE Status 0x20 = DONE_ATTN — server acknowledged attention signal

feature_ext_list.desc: Always last, no DataLen or Data

examples.token_stream: DONEINPROC* → ENVCHANGE* → INFO* → LOGINACK → FEATUREEXTACK → DONE

examples.name: Begin Transaction -> SQL Batch -> Commit (MARS-safe)

sequence.summary: ENVCHANGE type 8 returns transaction descriptor, e.g. 01 00 00 00 45 00 00 00, followed by DONE
SQLBatch uses ALL_HEADERS.TransactionDescriptor = 01 00 00 00 45 00 00 00 instead of zero
TransactionManagerRequest(TM_COMMIT_XACT) reuses the same descriptor in ALL_HEADERS
ENVCHANGE type 9/10/17 clears the descriptor; subsequent SQLBatch/RPC requests return to zero descriptor

notes: This example documents the failure mode fixed in sqlserver-nio: raw SQL BEGIN/COMMIT is insufficient under MARS unless the client also updates the transaction descriptor carried in ALL_HEADERS.
The exact descriptor bytes vary per session; the example uses 01 00 00 00 45 00 00 00 as a representative 8-byte descriptor learned from ENVCHANGE type 8.
